newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Senate to query pension fund payout limit.
newsitem.headline: French Senate to query pension fund payout limit.

text.p: The Senate may seek to amend a bill on introducing private pension funds in France, in particular to get rid of the 100,000-franc ($19,000) limit on lump sum payouts, but keeping the 20 percent lump-sum payout rule.
The bill goes to the Senate on Thursday, where there could also be a debate on a clause that would offer relief from Social Security payroll charges for employer contributions to pension funds.

Philippe Marini, the senator in charge of reporting on the bill and a member of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's RPR party, told Reuters the upper house of parliament would not be a simple rubber-stamping exercise.
"There will definitely be a fully-fledged debate" which will focus on "all the problems", he said.

Marini said he approved of the test adopted by the National Assembly on November 22 but that he favoured amendments that had been proposed by the finance committee and aimed at offering "greater security, transparency, greater wisdom and equity".

Marini said he approved of the percentage limit -- fixed at 20 percent -- for the amount people could take out in a lump sum at retirement age but believed the limit in absolute terms -- fixed at 100,000 francs -- was "unrealistic".

"What will 100,000 francs be in 30 or 40 years time. I'd prefer to stick with 20 percent," he said, adding that a limit in absolute terms would have to be re-evaluated every year and create "legislative instability".

Another amendment he said the senate was looking at allowed employees whose company was not in a pension plan to subscribe to another pension, in a move aimed at helping staff of small and medium sized companies.
-- William Emmanuel, Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.255 French Francs)
